content.content:
# Fleet baseline — force every member to baseline now

**This task runs no agent, and no schedule.** It is `frequency: manual` with `agent_model: none`: it never fires on any cadence, and the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) → [`force-fleet-baseline.mjs`](force-fleet-baseline.mjs) the scheduler runs as a subprocess when — and only when — a human forces it. This file is the human-facing record of what that is; there is no dispatch issue and no subagent.

## How to pull the lever

Run this repo's **Claudinite scheduler** workflow by hand (Actions → Claudinite scheduler → Run workflow) with `overrides`:

```
FORCE_TASKS=fleet-baseline
REPOS=Alpha Beta            ← optional: limit to these repos (bare name or owner/name, SPACE-separated); omit for every covered member
DRY_RUN=true                ← optional: report what would fire, fire nothing
INCLUDE_DORMANT=true        ← optional: dormant members are skipped by default — they stopped their own scheduler on purpose
```

Values are space-separated because the override bag splits `KEY=value` pairs on commas.

## What it does

Enumerate every repo under the configured owner over the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT and, for each **covered, non-dormant** member, fire that member's own `claudinite-scheduler.yml` with `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` — the same button the owner would press in that repo's Actions tab, pressed across the fleet in one run. A forced run evaluates **only** the forced task (engine contract, #749), so each member does exactly one thing: baseline.

Nothing is baselined *here*, and nothing is written to any member — no commit, no issue, no comment. Each member converges its own mount, with its own token, under its own scheduler and delivery policy; if its converge needs an agent, that member's own executor runs it. The enforcer **dispatches**; the member **executes**. That is the whole trust model: no agent anywhere needs cross-repo access, and the one fleet credential is the PAT with Actions write.

Every repo under the owner lands in the run summary under exactly one state — fired, canon, out-of-scope, excluded, filtered-out, uncovered, dormant, or failed — so a fleet-wide force is never mistaken for fleet-wide coverage.

## What it deliberately does not do

**It does not wait.** A dispatch queues a run; what that run went on to do is each member's own story, told where members always tell it — a maintenance PR, a dispatch issue, a failure escalation in that repo. The retired workflow's *follow* half (watch every member to a terminal state, render a fleet report) is what forced the lever to be a standalone workflow with a 45-minute sleep; giving it up is what lets the lever ride the ordinary scheduler. If a member's forced run went wrong, that member says so in its own repo.

## Why a task and not a workflow (any more)

The standalone `fleet-baseline.yml` workflow (retired 2026-08-11, #749) lived in the enforcer's `.github/` — the one place the nightly converge can never push (#649), so every change to it crossed the fleet by the slow withhold-and-hand-to-the-agent path. As a task, the lever ships with the ordinary vendor refresh like everything else, and the repo's vendored scheduler stays its **only** workflow. The typed `workflow_dispatch` inputs the old workflow offered are carried by the override bag above.

## Failure is loud

A member that could not be dispatched — a missing scheduler, a PAT without Actions write, a workflow GitHub disabled — is named in the summary under `failed`, and the sweep exits non-zero. The scheduler converges a `needs-human` issue for the task family, so a broken grant escalates rather than silently leaving part of the fleet unforced.

questions.question: Forcing the fleet is a fleet-wide effect, so I'm stopping for it. The lever is a `manual` task in **Sheepdog** (`FORCE_TASKS=fleet-baseline` on its scheduler workflow) — it dispatches every covered member's own scheduler with `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` and does **not** wait; each member converges under its own token and reports in its own repo. Two things worth knowing: this session's GitHub scope is Claudinite only, so reaching Sheepdog costs an `add_repo` (~4-5 min in this environment); and the `core-seed` record has a 7-day recency window, so the ordinary nightly converges will declare `core` fleet-wide anyway — forcing buys speed and same-session verification, not correctness. How do you want to proceed?

answers.Forcing the fleet is a fleet-wide effect: Attach Sheepdog and force it now

[Resource from github at repo://missingbulb/Sheepdog/sha/a9dd0f9c59fc4c31a0f7efd8c5f871492f35e2d4/contents/.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml] # Claudinite per-repo task scheduler — the repo's ONLY cron
# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; the update flows re-derive the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '10 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=update.'
        required: false
        default: ''

# Scheduled (and plain manual) runs serialize in one group so a slow run and its
# successor never overlap. A run carrying OVERRIDES gets a group of its own, keyed
# by run id: a forced run does exactly one named task, and the fleet fan-out case
# (an enforcer firing FORCE_TASKS at many members at once) must neither queue
# behind the hourly cron nor be silently dropped by it — GitHub keeps at most ONE
# pending run per group and cancels older pending ones, so a shared group can eat
# a forced dispatch without a trace. The (task, slot) exactly-once dispatch guard
# and the workers' idempotence are what make the rare overlap with a cron run safe.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler${{ inputs.overrides != '' && inputs.overrides != null && format('-forced-{0}', github.run_id) || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; the update runner pushes its delivery branch (task-prework §7/E4)
  issues: write          # file / label / close dispatch issues
  pull-requests: write   # the update runner opens the per-cycle PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # read the run ledger (last successful run) for due-slot math, AND
                         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (store-release fires the release
                         # orchestrator's daily leg) — creating a workflow_dispatch event needs
                         # write, not read, and `read` silently 403s the POST

jobs:
  schedule:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite scheduler run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

content.content:
7:Daily, over the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT: read this (sheepdog) repo's `sheepdog` pack entry `config` (`owner`, `exclude`, `canonRepo`, `staleDays`), read canon's default branch, enumerate every repo that owner owns, and walk it **once** — one declaration read per repo, plus two further reads (scheduler workflow, canon compare) for each member the freshness question actually measures.
20:These were two — a daily `fleet-census` and a weekly `fleet-freshness` — and each carried its own enumeration, its own owner filter, its own empty-enumeration guard, its own home/canon/archived/fork/excluded skips and its own declaration read per repo. The freshness half's header said it *"takes coverage as given"*, but it could not: the census's verdict lived in another process on another cadence, so it re-derived the whole thing.
22:That produced divergence in the classification itself. `exclude` was applied at different points, so an excluded repo that still carried a declaration read **covered** to one sweep and **out of scope** to the other. And each half's `unknown` failed its own run knowing nothing of the other's, so one green run beside one red one told a reader nothing about which half of the fleet picture to trust.
32:| `no-stamp` | declares packs but was never vendored — no engine on disk at all |
47:- **Canon** is an ordinary covered member to the coverage question (it carries a declaration) and is never measured by the freshness one (it has no vendored mount to be stale).
48:- **An excluded repo** that still carries a declaration is **covered** — saying otherwise would report a repo as missing something it has — and is **out of scope** for freshness, because upkeep is what the exclusion opted out of.
49:- **A dormant member** (`"dormant": true`, [the scheduler's gate](../../../core/scheduled-tasks.md)) is a covered member with no freshness verdict: its stamp is never read, and any open drift issue for it closes *not planned*. Its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls behind **by design**. The test is `isDormant`, re-exported from the engine rather than re-implemented — a sweep with a private notion of dormancy would nag exactly the repos that had already opted out.
59:Its *implementation* scans every repo under the owner, but its declaration, scheduling and lifecycle are those of **any pack task**: it is active because this repo declares the `sheepdog` pack, and it runs on this repo's ordinary scheduler. It declares no `fleet` signal and no `fleet` session scope — the cross-repo reach lives in the implementation, never in the wiring.
63:A repo whose **declaration** cannot be read or parsed is `unknown` to **both** questions — it is the input they share. A repo whose **mount probe** fails (the scheduler read, canon's compare) is `unknown` to the **freshness** question alone: the coverage question already read that declaration successfully and keeps its verdict.

content.content:
# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at http://[REDACTED:env:CLOUDSDK_PROXY_ADDRESS]:45807
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
[REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS http://[REDACTED:env:CLOUDSDK_PROXY_ADDRESS]:45807/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at [REDACTED:env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS]
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

### "405 Method Not Allowed" from the proxy

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for

input.body:
Phase 1 landed in #836 (`d067b25`). This is the follow-up the two-phase split in #835 was for.

## Why it waited

A member runs the self-refresh from its **vendored** copy at `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/update/`, and `discoverTasks` finds only a task whose pack is *literally* declared. Moving the directory before every member's declaration carries `core` leaves that member with no update task and nothing able to deliver it one.

## Fleet force — 2026-08-14 22:16Z

Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` lever ([run 31845961312](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/actions/runs/31845961312)): **11 fired, 5 skipped, 0 failed.**

Read-back of each member's own `.claudinite-checks.json`, off a fresh clone of its default branch:

| Member | `core` declared | engine | `core` version |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClaudiniteCanary | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| CrosswordChat | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| LaughCounter | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| Sheepdog | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| TLDR | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| VascularColoring | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| Claudinite (home) | ✅ | — | — |
| EdFringeNow | ⏳ **on its delivery branch, not on `main`** | 3 → 4 on the branch | 1 on the branch |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |
| MissingbulbWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |

The seed record and the `requires` closure both did exactly what #836 claimed: every member that completed a converge declares `core` at version 1.

## Three things to close before moving the task

- [ ] **EdFringeNow's delivery is parked.** Its converge ran and is correct — `claudinite/update-2026-08-14-o6413o` carries `core`, engine 4, `core: 1` — but the PR never merged, and the repo is still on engine 3, so it also missed #837. Pre-existing and not caused by #836. Needs a look in that repo before its `tasks/update` moves.
- [ ] **Two private members were unverifiable.** `ClaudiniteWebsite` and `MissingbulbWebsite` are private, so anonymous reads 404 and direct `api.github.com` is denied by the session's egress policy. Both were fired successfully; neither is *confirmed*. Verify with a session that has them attached, or via a fleet sweep that reports declarations.
- [ ] **Dormant members will never receive `core` on the current carrier.** `EdFringeAllocator`, `Gratio` and `HelloWorldFlutterApp` are self-declared dormant and were skipped. `core` is a new pack, so no member carries an installed version for it, and `migrationApplies` falls back to the 7-day recency window — past 2026-08-21 the `core-seed` record stops applying to any repo that has not converged. A dormant member that wakes after that gets `core`'s *content* through the `requires` closure but never the *declaration*, so the pack is mounted and inert and `core-declared` cannot report it (it does not run when `core` is undeclared).

The durable fix for the third is Sheepdog's `packSeeds` — its `sheepdog` pack config already seeds `claude-code-web-users-support` this way, and the `fleet-pack-seeds` sweep has no recency window. Adding `core` there is a one-line config change in Sheepdog, and is the owner's call since it writes to members.

## Then

1. `git mv packs/basics/tasks/update packs/core/tasks/update`, with the manifest comments that reference it.
2. Promote `core-declared` from advisory to blocking (one line in `packs/core/core-declared.mjs`).
3. Force the fleet again and read back.

- **EdFringeNow converged correctly but its delivery is parked.** Its branch `claudinite/update-2026-08-14-o6413o` carries `core`, engine 4, `core: 1` — the PR just never merged, which is why the repo also still lacks engine 4 from [#837](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/837). Pre-existing, not caused by this change. I'm deliberately not naming a cause; the two reads that would settle it are behind the API.
- **Two private members are unverifiable from this session.** `ClaudiniteWebsite` and `MissingbulbWebsite` were fired successfully, but anonymous reads 404 on private repos and `api.github.com` is denied by the egress policy. That's a policy boundary, so I stopped rather than routing around it — they are *unconfirmed*, not *failed*.
- **A real gap my own design left.** Dormant members will never get `core`. Because it's a new pack, no member has an installed version for it, so `migrationApplies` falls back to the 7-day recency window — after 2026-08-21 the seed record stops applying to any repo that hasn't converged. A dormant member waking later gets `core`'s content via the closure but never the declaration, leaving it mounted and inert, and `core-declared` can't report that because it doesn't run when `core` is undeclared. The durable carrier is Sheepdog's `packSeeds`, which has no recency window and already seeds `claude-code-web-users-support` that way — one line of Sheepdog config, but it writes to members, so it's yours.

One process note: my earlier CI monitor never fired because `curl` to `api.github.com` returns 403 through the proxy. I'd been reading that as "still running". The MCP tools are the working channel; `raw.githubusercontent` works but is CDN-stale, which briefly made Sheepdog look like it hadn't converged when it had.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#842](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/842)** holds phase 2 and its three preconditions. I'd suggest taking the dormant-member gap first — it's the one that fails silently, and its window closes 2026-08-21. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.

## Why it waited

A member runs the self-refresh from its **vendored** copy at `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/update/`, and `discoverTasks` finds only a task whose pack is *literally* declared. Moving the directory before every member's declaration carries `core` leaves that member with no update task and nothing able to deliver it one.

## Fleet force — 2026-08-14 22:16Z

Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` lever ([run 31845961312](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/actions/runs/31845961312)): **11 fired, 5 skipped, 0 failed.** Read-back off a fresh clone of each member's default branch, re-confirmed 22:35Z:

| Sheepdog | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| TLDR | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| VascularColoring | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| Claudinite (home) | ✅ | — | — |
| EdFringeNow | ⏳ on its delivery branch, not on `main` | 3 → 4 on the branch | 1 on the branch |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |
| MissingbulbWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |
| EdFringeAllocator, Gratio, HelloWorldFlutterApp | ❌ dormant — skipped, never fired | | |

The seed record and the `requires` closure both did exactly what #836 claimed: every member that completed a converge declares `core` at version 1.

## Three things to close before moving the task

- [ ] **EdFringeNow's delivery is parked.** Its converge ran and is correct — `claudinite/update-2026-08-14-o6413o` carries `core`, engine 4, `core: 1` — but the PR never merged, and the repo is still on engine 3, so it also missed #837. Pre-existing and not caused by #836. Needs a look in that repo.
- [ ] **Two private members were unverifiable.** `ClaudiniteWebsite` and `MissingbulbWebsite` are private, so anonymous reads 404 and direct `api.github.com` is denied by the session's egress policy. Both were fired successfully; neither is *confirmed*.
- [ ] **The three dormant members will never receive `core` on the current carrier, and phase 2 would wedge them.** `core` is a new pack, so no member carries an installed version for it, and `migrationApplies` falls back to the 7-day recency window — **past 2026-08-21 the `core-seed` record stops applying to any repo that has not converged**. input.body:
Phase 1 landed in #836 (`d067b25`). This is the follow-up the two-phase split in #835 was for.

## Why it waited

A member runs the self-refresh from its **vendored** copy at `.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/update/`, and `discoverTasks` finds only a task whose pack is *literally* declared. Moving the directory before every member's declaration carries `core` leaves that member with no update task and nothing able to deliver it one.

## Fleet force — 2026-08-14 22:16Z

Sheepdog's `fleet-baseline` lever ([run 31845961312](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/actions/runs/31845961312)): **11 fired, 5 skipped, 0 failed.** Read-back off a fresh clone of each member's default branch:

| Member | `core` declared | engine | `core` version |
|---|---|---|---|
| ClaudiniteCanary | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| CrosswordChat | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| EdFringeNow | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| LaughCounter | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| Sheepdog | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| TLDR | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| VascularColoring | ✅ | 4 | 1 |
| Claudinite (home) | ✅ | — | — |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |
| MissingbulbWebsite | ❔ private — unverifiable from that session | | |
| EdFringeAllocator, Gratio, HelloWorldFlutterApp | ❌ dormant — skipped, never fired | | |

**9 of 11 fired members confirmed, plus the home.** The seed record and the `requires` closure both did exactly what #836 claimed: every member that completed a converge declares `core` at version 1.

## Open before moving the task

- [ ] **Two private members are unverified.** `ClaudiniteWebsite` and `MissingbulbWebsite` are private, so anonymous reads 404 and direct `api.github.com` is denied by the session's egress policy. Both were fired successfully; neither is *confirmed*. Verify from a session with them attached, or via a fleet sweep that reports declarations.

## Closed — EdFringeNow was a flaky golden, not a parked run

Its update PR ([EdFringeNow#355](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/355)) sat unmerged because `ui-requirements` failed **96/97** on one screenshot golden — `now-plan-strip.4.4` ("a selected show that breaks the commitment wears the You'll-be-late chip"). `ci` passed; `main`'s own last run was green; the PR touches only the vendored mount, which cannot reach that suite. Re-running the failed job with no code change went green, confirming flake. Merged as `1a385ec`; `main` now reads `core`, engine 4, `core: 1`.

Two things worth carrying:

- **The first read was wrong, and the right one was cheap.** This looked like the known parked-`action_required` shape, where checks never report. It wasn't — they reported, and one failed. Two API reads (check runs on the PR, then `main`'s history) separated the two in under a minute. Symptom-matching to a remembered failure mode is what cost the time.
- **Auto-merge was never armed.** `updated_at` never moved from the PR's creation minute, so nothing re-evaluated when the checks went green — the PR would have sat indefinitely even after the flake cleared. That is the same "counts dispatches, not outcomes" blindness the canon already tracks: the run reported a successful delivery, and one flaky test turned it into a repo silently a day behind. Worth its own issue if it recurs on another member.

## Settled — the dormant three, accepted wedge

**Owner decision, 2026-08-14: leave the dormant members dormant and accept the repair cost if one wakes. Phase 2 proceeds without them.** Do not re-propose forcing them.

The mechanism, recorded so whoever meets it knows what they are looking at: `core` is a new pack, so no member carries an installed version for it, and `migrationApplies` falls back to the 7-day recency window — **after 2026-08-21 the `core-seed` record stops applying to any repo that has not converged**. `EdFringeAllocator`, `Gratio` and `HelloWorldFlutterApp` are self-declared dormant and were never fired, so none of them has it.

If one of them wakes after that date: it gets `core`'s *content* through the `requires` closure but never the *declaration*. The pack is mounted and inert, `core-declared` cannot report it (it does not run when `core` is undeclared), and once phase 2 has moved `tasks/update` into `core` that repo has **no update task and nothing able to deliver it one**. The repair is one manual edit — add `"core"` to its `.claudinite-checks.json` `packs` array — after which its next scheduler run converges normally.

There is no standing carrier that would have avoided this. Sheepdog's `packSeeds` does not reach dormant members either: `fleet-pack-seeds` skips them by design — *"a member that declares `dormant: true` is one the sweep writes nothing to"* — same as `fleet-baseline`. Reaching a dormant repo requires deliberately overriding its opt-out, which is the thing being declined here.

## Then

1. `git mv packs/basics/tasks/update packs/core/tasks/update`, with the manifest comments that reference it.
2. Promote `core-declared` from advisory to blocking (one line in `packs/core/core-declared.mjs`).
3. Force the fleet again and read back.

13	Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
14	converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
15	not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.
16	
17	| Rule | Severity | What goes wrong when it fires |
18	|---|---|---|

20	| `rules-index-current` | blocking | the generated index is missing, stale or unimported — the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session |
21	| `claudinite-isolation` | blocking | the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` [barrier](../barriers/README.md) edge) |

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# core

Claudinite's own surface in a repo that runs it: the vendored mount, the declaration that activates a
pack, adopting Claudinite and adopting a pack, and the contract every scheduled task is written to.

**Mandatory.** `basics` `requires` this pack, so the closure vendors its content and materializes its
declaration wherever a declaration is written; the one-time `core-seed` migration record declares it
into members that already exist. Removing the entry is not an opt-out — it is drift, and `core-declared`
reports it.

## Checks

Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.

| Rule | Severity | What goes wrong when it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `core-declared` | advisory | this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-checks.json`, so none of the rules below run and the session cannot tell |
| `rules-index-current` | blocking | the generated index is missing, stale or unimported — the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session |
| `claudinite-isolation` | blocking | the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` [barrier](../barriers/README.md) edge) |
| `conformance-workflow` | advisory | nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands |
| `scheduler-workflow-shape` | blocking | the vendored scheduler's cron, concurrency or dispatch guard has drifted — staggering, double-run safety or manual runs break |
| `task-declaration-shape` | blocking | a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal, so the task never fires or fires wrong |
| `task-declaration-matches-folder` | blocking | a declaration disagrees with its folder — discovery drops it into `errors` and every run keeps reporting healthy without it |
| `task-phase-discipline` | advisory | a task decides not to run after its precondition already said run, hiding the decision from the run records |

The scope cuts the other way too: a rule about how the **canon's own** content is maintained is not
this pack's, however much it looks like one. `catalog-completeness` — `packs/README.md` lists every
`packs/<name>/` — reads as Claudinite machinery and is not: it can only fire in the corpus repo, and
what it guards is a hand-maintained index, not a member's status. It stays in
[basics](../basics/README.md) with the other doc-integrity rules.

## Skills

| Skill | For |
|---|---|
| [`adopt-claudinite`](skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md) | setting a project up on Claudinite for the first time — mount, hooks, checks, skills — and re-baselining one to pick up updates |
| [`adopt-pack`](skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) | adding a pack to a repo that already runs Claudinite: declare, interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land |

`adopt-claudinite` bundles two more checks of the same kind — `adoption-answers-pending` and
`interview-answer-stale`, over the answers a member stores against each declared pack's questions.

## Tasks

| Task | frequency | Runs when |
|---|---|---|
| `adopt-requested-packs` | daily | the repo carries an open pack-adoption request |

The `update` self-refresh task is still `basics`' (`packs/core/tasks/update/`) and moves here in a
second change, once every member's declaration is confirmed to carry `core`. A member runs that task
from its **vendored** copy, and `discoverTasks` only finds a task whose pack is literally declared —
so moving the directory before the declaration has landed everywhere would leave a member with no
update task at all, and nothing left that could deliver it one.

11	## Checks

13	Each of these asks the same kind of question: **is Claudinite working in this repo** — declared,
14	converged, gated, scheduled. A repo can fail any of them silently, which is why they are checks and
15	not prose: the session that has lost its rules is the session least able to notice.

18	|---|---|---|
19	| `core-declared` | blocking | this pack's entry is gone from `.claudinite-checks.json`, so none of the rules below run and the session cannot tell |
20	| `rules-index-current` | blocking | the generated index is missing, stale or unimported — the repo's packs contribute no prose to any session |
21	| `claudinite-isolation` | blocking | the repo's own code reaches into `.claudinite/`, so the next canon refactor is a breaking migration for code the canon does not own (a declared `forbidReferences` [barrier](../barriers/README.md) edge) |
22	| `conformance-workflow` | advisory | nothing in CI runs the world sweep unfiltered on a pull request, so conformance is ungated and the maintenance PR never lands |

24	| `task-declaration-shape` | blocking | a task declaration the scheduler reads is incomplete or illegal, so the task never fires or fires wrong |
25	| `task-declaration-matches-folder` | blocking | a declaration disagrees with its folder — discovery drops it into `errors` and every run keeps reporting healthy without it |

input.body:
Closes #842. Phase 1 was #836.

`basics/tasks/update/` → `core/tasks/update/`, and `core-declared` advisory → blocking.

## Why this waited, and what released it

A member runs the self-refresh from its **vendored** copy, and `discoverTasks` finds only a *literally-declared* pack's tasks. Moving the directory before every member declared `core` would have left that member with no update task and nothing able to deliver it one — the one failure the two-phase split existed to prevent.

That precondition is now met and **read back rather than assumed**. The forced pass of 2026-08-14 ([Sheepdog run 31845961312](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/actions/runs/31845961312), 11 fired / 5 skipped / 0 failed) put the declaration in **all 11 non-dormant members plus the canon home**, each confirmed individually against its own `.claudinite-checks.json`, all at `core: 1` on engine 4.

The last member to confirm, EdFringeNow, is worth a line: its update PR sat unmerged on a **flaky** golden (`ui-requirements`, 96/97, `now-plan-strip.4.4`). A re-run with no code change went green. It was not the parked-`action_required` shape it resembled — the checks did report, one failed — and its auto-merge was never armed, so it would have sat there even after the flake cleared.

## `core-declared` → blocking

It shipped advisory on the `conformance-workflow` precedent: blocking from the start would have turned every member red before the seed record reached it. That reason is spent. And this change raises the stakes it guards — a missing declaration now costs a member its **self-refresh**, not just its rules — so the two belong in one commit.

## The dormant three — a known, accepted gap

Owner decision, 2026-08-14: `EdFringeAllocator`, `Gratio` and `HelloWorldFlutterApp` are self-declared dormant, were never forced, and do not carry the declaration. After 2026-08-21 the `core-seed` record's recency window closes, so a repo that wakes later gets `core`'s *content* through the `requires` closure but never the *declaration* — leaving the pack mounted and inert, its update task undiscoverable, and `core-declared` unable to report it (it does not run when the pack is undeclared).

The repair is one manual edit: add `"core"` to that repo's `packs` array. It is written at the rule itself rather than left to be rediscovered, because the rule is structurally incapable of saying it.

## Sheepdog's forced-task guard

`force-fleet-baseline.test.mjs` pinned `FORCED_TASK` against `packs/basics/tasks/<id>/task.mjs` — it went red on this move. Rather than swapping the pack name, it now asserts **exactly one pack owns the id**: which pack holds `update` is not the lever's business and has changed once already, while "no pack owns this id" is the failure it exists to catch (a dispatch into nothing that still reports success, Sheepdog#172).

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1674 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 28 advisory**, unchanged from the base.
- `engine/selftest.mjs --strict` — 5 probes pass.
- `discoverTasks` against the home's real declaration resolves **`core/update`**, 0 errors.
- `computeVendorSet(['basics'])` still lays down the update task's 3 files — the `requires` closure carries it to a member that names only `basics`.
- Every `tasks/update` reference in the tree points at `core`, including the canary-rehearsal workflow's `working-directory` and the escaped-regex assertion that guards it.

The gate closed and phase 2 is up.

**Both private members confirmed** — `ClaudiniteWebsite` and `MissingbulbWebsite` each declare `core`, engine 4, `core: 1`. That makes it **11 of 11 fired members plus this repo**, every one read back individually.

**Phase 2 is [#844](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/844):** `basics/tasks/update/` → `core/tasks/update/`, and `core-declared` promoted to blocking. Those belong in one commit — the promotion's justification is precisely that a missing declaration now costs a member its self-refresh, not just its rules.

Two things the work turned up that I handled rather than worked around:

- **Sheepdog's forced-task guard went red**, and correctly — it pinned `FORCED_TASK` against `packs/basics/tasks/<id>/`. I didn't swap the pack name; it now asserts *exactly one pack owns the id*. Which pack holds `update` isn't the lever's business and has already changed once, while "no pack owns this id" is the real failure it guards against — a dispatch into nothing that still reports success.

input.body:
Closes #842. Phase 1 was #836.

`basics/tasks/update/` → `core/tasks/update/`, and `core-declared` advisory → blocking.

## Why this waited, and what released it

A member runs the self-refresh from its **vendored** copy, and `discoverTasks` finds only a *literally-declared* pack's tasks. Moving the directory before every member declared `core` would have left that member with no update task and nothing able to deliver it one — the one failure the two-phase split existed to prevent.

That precondition is now met and **read back rather than assumed**. The forced pass of 2026-08-14 ([Sheepdog run 31845961312](https://github.com/missingbulb/Sheepdog/actions/runs/31845961312), 11 fired / 5 skipped / 0 failed) put the declaration in **all 11 non-dormant members plus the canon home**, each confirmed individually against its own `.claudinite-checks.json`, all at `core: 1` on engine 4.

The last member to confirm, EdFringeNow, is worth a line: its update PR sat unmerged on a **flaky** golden (`ui-requirements`, 96/97, `now-plan-strip.4.4`). A re-run with no code change went green. It was not the parked-`action_required` shape it resembled — the checks did report, one failed — and its auto-merge was never armed, so it would have sat there even after the flake cleared.

## `core-declared` → blocking

It shipped advisory on the `conformance-workflow` precedent: blocking from the start would have turned every member red before the seed record reached it. That reason is spent. And this change raises the stakes it guards — a missing declaration now costs a member its **self-refresh**, not just its rules — so the two belong in one commit.

### Consumer safety: the fixture, and why not a record

`consumer-safe-change` flagged the severity change. **The fixture is the honest answer, not a migration record**, because the rule is structurally incapable of turning a member red: activation reads the literal `packs` list, so in the one repo shape where `core-declared` would fire, it does not run at all. A record would have nothing to move.

That was an argument, and the fixtures made it a weak one — **every fixture declared `basics` and not `core`**, so they all modelled the shape the fleet no longer has, in the direction that hides a regression: the `requires` closure vendors core's content either way, so the mount looks complete while `isActive` reads false and every rule and task the pack owns silently does not run. Two changes:

- `core` is prepended to every fixture's declaration, matching what the forced pass actually produced in the fleet.
- **`core-undeclared`** pins the un-migrated shape once, deliberately, instead of it being every fixture's accidental default. It is the shape the three dormant repos are frozen in, and it must converge green — with its own comment recording that green there means *"not broken by the severity"*, never *"fully functional"*: it has no update task since the move.

Verified in both directions rather than asserted — pointing the rule's constant at a pack no fixture declares turns **every** `core`-declaring fixture red, while `core-undeclared` stays green throughout.

## The dormant three — a known, accepted gap

Owner decision, 2026-08-14: `EdFringeAllocator`, `Gratio` and `HelloWorldFlutterApp` are self-declared dormant, were never forced, and do not carry the declaration. After 2026-08-21 the `core-seed` record's recency window closes, so a repo that wakes later gets `core`'s *content* through the `requires` closure but never the *declaration* — leaving the pack mounted and inert, its update task undiscoverable, and `core-declared` unable to report it.

The repair is one manual edit: add `"core"` to that repo's `packs` array. It is written at the rule itself rather than left to be rediscovered, because the rule is structurally incapable of saying it.

## Sheepdog's forced-task guard

`force-fleet-baseline.test.mjs` pinned `FORCED_TASK` against `packs/basics/tasks/<id>/task.mjs` — it went red on this move. Rather than swapping the pack name, it now asserts **exactly one pack owns the id**: which pack holds `update` is not the lever's business and has changed once already, while "no pack owns this id" is the failure it exists to catch (a dispatch into nothing that still reports success, Sheepdog#172).

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **1676 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking**; the one advisory on the branch is pre-existing `rules-line-length` in a file already listed in #766, and this branch's edits to it only shortened lines.

Both blocking findings are fixed, and the second one was worth catching.

**`consumer-safe-change` was right and my reasoning was too comfortable.** I'd argued `core-declared` can't turn a member red — activation reads the literal declaration, so in the one shape where it would fire, it doesn't run. That's true, but it was an argument, not evidence. Chasing it down made it worse: **every rehearsal fixture declared `basics` and not `core`**, so they all modelled the shape the fleet no longer has — and in the direction that hides a regression. The `requires` closure vendors core's content either way, so the mount looks complete while `isActive` reads false and everything the pack owns silently doesn't run. My phase-2 change would have moved the update task into a pack that no fixture activated.

So: `core` now leads every fixture's declaration, matching what the forced pass actually produced, and a new **`core-undeclared`** fixture pins the un-migrated shape once, deliberately, rather than it being every fixture's accidental default. It carries its own warning that green there means *"not broken by the severity"*, never *"fully functional"* — that member has no update task since the move.

I verified both directions instead of trusting the green: pointing the rule's constant at a pack no fixture declares turns **every** `core`-declaring fixture red, while `core-undeclared` stays green throughout. A fixture that can't fail proves nothing.

I chose the fixture over a migration record and said so in the PR — a record would have nothing to move, since no member's file needs changing for this severity.

One advisory remains on the branch: `rules-line-length` on `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md`. It's pre-existing (fires identically with my work stashed), my two edits there only *shortened* lines, and it's already tracked in [#766](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/766), which lists that exact file at longest 128. Left alone rather than duplicated.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#844](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/844) awaits your review** — 1676 tests pass, 0 blocking, and the severity change is now rehearsed against a consumer in both directions. On `lgtm` I'll merge and force the fleet, so the moved update task is exercised on real members rather than assumed — that force is the only thing that proves a member can still refresh itself from its new home.
